text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Moslem-Croat Federation House of Representatives was due to hold a session on Thursday but it was postponed until May 5 because of disputes over the establishment of new municipalities, the paper said.
- An international business fair, "Promo 97", opens in Tuzla. A total of 366 companies from 13 countries are taking part in the event.

- A group of 420 election supervisors should arrive in Bosnia this weekend, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said. They will monitor voter registration in upcoming local elections in September.

- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia Kasim Trnka denies report in Belgrade newspaper that he expected a meeting between Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic and chairman of Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic.
- Top officials in Mostar and international representatives discuss financing of city administration by the World Bank. Croat mayor Ivan Prskalo calls World Bank's conditions unfavourable.
- Meteorological office of Bosnia said weather this April is the coldest in 100 years.
- Croat mayor of Mostar, Ivan Prskalo, said that he stands by his statement that Mostar is "Our town, the Croat town of Mostar" which he gave at opening of music festival.
- Zenica mines produced 44,000 tons of coal in the first quarter of this year, and a further 300,000 tons are expected by the end of the year.
- No incidents were reported during the Islamic holiday of Bairam last week, when about 100 visits to graveyards were organised, United Nations spokesman says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
